answer: Rate-limited reward vesting forces every new agent identity to wait before extracting value. When an agent completes a task, payment doesn't arrive at once—it flows through a jetty of time-locked escrow stages over weeks. A sybil attacker spawning a thousand hollow identities pays compute and registration costs immediately but must sustain those identities through the entire vesting period to reach the oasis of actual liquidity. The attack becomes a cash-flow trap: upfront costs multiply by farm size while income trickles in slowly, making mass identity creation economically unviable.
